{{nihongo|'''Oyatsuhime Shrine'''|大屋都姫神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kii Province]].

'''Deity enshrined''
* Left Wakimiya: {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|Isotakeru-no-kami|zh|五十猛神|qid=Q10881556|lt=Goju Takekami}} (Itakeru Mikoto)

* Right side shrine: {{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|ja|オオヤツヒメ・ツマツヒメ|zh|大屋津姬命與枛津姬命|qid=Q10935047|lt=Miyatomatohime no Mikoto}} (Tsumatsuhime no Mikoto)
*: The sister deity of Oyatsu Hime no Mikoto, and the enshrined deity {{ill|Tsumatsuhime Shrine|Q17216259|qid=Q17216259}}.As the company name suggests, our company is said to be a shrine dedicated to '''{{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|ja|オオヤツヒメ・ツマツヒメ|zh|大屋津姬命與枛津姬命|qid=Q10935047|lt=Ooyatsuhime}}''' (Oyatsuhime no Mikoto). Regarding Ooyatsuhime, in the 5th book of the ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}'' Jindaiki's Treasure Sword Appearance Stage (8th Stage of the First Jindai Period), it is described that she is the daughter god of {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo}} (Susanoo). Also, the older brother god of Ooyatsuhime is {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|Isotakeru-no-kami|zh|五十猛神|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru/Itakeru}}, and the younger sister god is {{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|ja|オオヤツヒメ・ツマツヒメ|zh|大屋津姬命與枛津姬命|qid=Q10935047|lt=Sakutsuhime no Mikoto}} (Tsumatsu Both gods are currently enshrined at {{ill|Itakiso shrine|ja|伊太祁曽神社|zh|伊太祁曾神社|qid=Q11379271}} (Itaikiso, Wakayama City) and {{ill|Tsumatsuhime Shrine|Q17216259|qid=Q17216259}} (3 Ronsha shrines), respectively. These three deities are said to be the gods who brought tree seeds to Kii Province, and in Kii they are collectively known as ``''Itae Sosanjin'''' {{Sfn|Oyatsuhime Shrine (Taira)|1983|p=444-445}}. Furthermore, in the Jigihonki, ``{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751}}'', these three gods are said to be the gods enshrined by {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11604953|qid=Q11604953}}.According to the shrine's legend, there was once a vast forest in the area around our company, and the wood was used to build houses, so it was given the divine name of ``Oya.'' According to "{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}", the name of the enshrined place, "Udamori", came from the company's shrine complex.{{Sfn|Oyatsuhime Shrine (corner)|1985}}.

== History ==

=== Founding ===Founding date is unknown. Shrine biography<ref group="Hara" name="Furuyu">"Shrine Furyu" ({{Harvtxt|Oyatsuhime Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1987|p=46-47}}). </ref> According to .94|N|135|12|4.67|E|region:JP-30_type:landmark|Location|name=Maezen Shrine/Kokake Shrine (first enshrined place?①)}}) It was originally enshrined in the ground, but in {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, the site was given to Ryojingu Shrine in 1616 and renamed to the ``Boar Forest'' in Shandong (Itaikeso, Wakayama City, {{Wiki coordinates|34|1 1|58.42|N|135|15|14.38|E|region:JP-30_type:landmark|location|name=Boar Forest (former enshrined place?②)}})<ref group="Note">Currently, Sansei Shrine, a shrine outside the precincts of {{ill|Itakiso shrine|ja|伊太祁曽神社|zh|伊太祁曾神社|qid=Q11379271}}, is located in Ino no Mori. </ref>{{Sfn|Oyatsuhime Shrine (corner)|1985}}. After that, "{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}" written by <ref group="Hara" name="Taiho"/> {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} In the 2nd year ({{ill|702|ab|702|af|702|am|702 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|702|ar|702|ary|702|ast|702|az|702|azb|۷۰۲ (میلادی)|bar|702|be|702|be_x_old|702|bg|702|bn|৭০২|bpy|মারি ৭০২|br|702|bs|702.|ca|702|cdo|702 nièng|ceb|702|ckb|٧٠٢|crh|702|cs|702|cv|702|cy|702|da|702|de|702|el|702|eml|702|eo|702|es|702|et|702|eu|702|fa|۷۰۲ (میلادی)|fi|702|fo|702|fr|702|frr|702|fy|702|ga|702|gan|702年|gd|702|gl|702|he|702|hi|702|hr|702.|ht|702 (almanak jilyen)|hu|702|hy|702|id|702|ilo|702|io|702|is|702|it|702|ja|702年|jv|702|ka|702|kaa|702|kk|702 жыл|ko|702년|la|702|lb|702|lij|702|lmo|702|lt|702 m.|map_bms|702|mdf|702|mg|702|mhr|702|mk|702|mr|इ.स. ७०२|mrj|702 и|ms|702|mzn|۷۰۲|nah|702|nap|702|nds|702|new|सन् ७०२|nl|702|nn|702|no|702|nrm|702|nso|702|oc|702|or|୭୦୨|os|702-æм аз|pl|702|pnb|702|pt|702|qu|702|ro|702|ru|702 год|rue|702|sa|७०२|scn|702|sd|702ع|sh|702.|shn|702|si|702|sk|702|sl|702|sq|702|sr|702|su|702|sv|702|sw|702|tg|Соли 702|th|พ.ศ. 1245|tk|702|tl|702|tly|702|tr|702|tt|702 ел|uk|702|ur|702ء|uz|702|vec|702|vi|702|war|702|wuu|702年|xmf|702|zh|702年|zh_min_nan|702 nî|zh_yue|702年|qid=Q23497}}), the three shrines of Ita-Kiso, Oyatsuhime, and Tomatuhime were transferred from Ino-no-Mori to the old shrine north of the current shrine site (Kitano-no-miya, Wakayama City). Mount Hara, {{Wiki coordinates|34|16|17.9|N|135|15|2.4|E|region:JP-30_type:landmark|location|name=Old palace (former enshrined place or ③)}}) <ref group="Note">There are currently no remains of the old palace. </ref>, and later relocated to its current location.{{Sfn|Oyatsuhime Shrine (corner)|1985}}<ref group="Note">In the Kii Famous Places Zue, ``Mt. Mihara'' is written as ``Mt. Miharayama'', and there is a different legend that it is the place where the three Ita-kami deities descended from the heavens with the seeds of wood, and from there they were divided into different shrines. </ref>.Also, "Oyatsu Hime-sha Engi" cited in "Zoku Fudoki" <ref group="Hara"> "Kii Zoku Fudoki". In </ref>, I will post a separate story that states that the three Itaige deities chose their respective places to be enshrined from Tenuki Bridge (bridge of the heavenly world) and went to various places {{ill|Amakudari|Q480175|qid=Q480175|lt=Amakudari}}, but Ōyatsuhime no Mikoto chose Hirata-go, descended there, ran a palace there, and was enshrined there.

Although its relationship with our company is unknown, to the east of the shrine there is the Udamori Ruins, which is thought to be a {{ill|Moated settlements|Q60995739|qid=Q60995739|lt=ring-moat village ruins}} from the middle of the {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}}.

=== After the Middle Ages ===
According to the shrine biography <ref group="Hara" name="Koyu"/>, it declined after suffering from the {{ill|Daiei (era)|Q1193564|qid=Q1193564}} uprising (first half of the 16th century) and the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} military fire ({{ill|Battle of Kishuu|Q10855721|qid=Q10855721|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Kishu Attack}}).

According to "Kanbunki" cited in "{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}", in the early modern period it had two towns of Kanda (approximately 2 hectares). Although this Kanda existed until after the war, it is said to have disappeared due to {{ill|Land reform|Q208128|qid=Q208128}} in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}21 ({{ill|1946|Q18610|qid=Q18610}}). group="Note">However, in Kanbunki, it is written in the past tense, ``existed until recent times (omitted).'' </ref>. In addition, the same article mentions that the area around our company, approximately 500 {{ill|Koku|Q855048|qid=Q855048|lt=stone}}, is called the ``Kami no Ki'' and is thought to be the remains of a vast shrine complex from ancient times, but the details are not clear. In "{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}," the company at the time was the birthplace deity of the two villages of Udamori and Kitano, but it was originally considered to have been the birthplace deity of the entire Hirata Manor to which these two villages belonged, and it is assumed that due to the separation of the Konishi, Nishitai, and Kita villages due to a conflict within the manor, only the two villages became the birthplace.In April of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} |Q134917284}}, and in 1880|Q7806}}, it was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}} {{Sfn|Oyatsuhime Shrine (corner)|1985}}. Also, in 1911|Q2076}}, the Soja Shrine (formerly Village Shrine) located in Miyanoshi in the northern part of Wakayama City was {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}} {{Sfn|Soja Shrine Ruins (Taira)|1983|p=443}} (described later). After the war, it belonged to {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ca|Associació de Santuaris Xinto|fr|Association des sanctuaires shinto|id|Asosiasi Kuil Shinto|it|Associazione dei santuari shintoisti|ja|神社本庁|ko|신사본청|ru|Дзиндзя хонтё|simple|Association of Shinto Shrines|sv|Jinja Honcho|zh|神社本廳|qid=Q908077}}.

== About Soja Shrine, a joint shrine ==
Oyatsuhime Shrine is the Sosha Shrine (formerly Village Shrine) located in Miyanoshi, Kita Aza, Wakayama City, which was enshrined in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}44 ({{ill|1911|Q2076|qid=Q2076}}). This Soja Shrine is a shrine that was also called ``Soja Daimyojin'' in early modern times, but the deity it enshrines is not clear (in ``Ki Meisho Zue'' it is said that {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nippon Takeru}} is enshrined) {{Sfn|Soja Shrine Ruins (Taira)|1983|p=443}}.

{{ill|Enkyō (Edo period)|Q1183728|qid=Q1183728}} 3 ({{ill|1746|Q7589|qid=Q7589}}) "Nanki Shrine Record" and its subsequent "Ki Meisho Zue" indicate that the shrine name and enshrinement location is "Soja" in Kii. |Q1629088}} is close to the estimated location (present-day Fuchu, Wakayama City), so this Soja Shrine is believed to be {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}} in Kii Province.{{Sfn|Soja Shrine Ruins (Taira)|1983|p=443}}. On the other hand, ``Kii Zoku Fudoki'' denies this and states that the shrine that was enshrined in Nezuku Valley in Taisho Ochiai Village (present-day Ochiai, Wakayama City) was transferred from the Sōron of the Shōchu period {{Sfn|Soja Shrine Ruins (Taira)|1983|p=443}}.

== Precincts ==
[[File:Oyatsuhime-jinja shaden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shrine building]]
As for the shrine building, the central main hall has an Oji-zukuri copper plate roof, {{ill|kōhai|Q11415970|qid=Q11415970}} is {{ill|Karahafu|Q977293|qid=Q977293|lt=kenkara gable}}, and {{jal {{Sfn|Oyatsuhime Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987|p=46-47}} where {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chigi}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuoki}} are placed in the ridge of ink|Shinsha}}. To keep out the fog, all four sides of the shrine are covered with wooden walls.

The side shrines on the left and right are also small-sized {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684}} with copper plate roofing and have chigi and bonito trees {{Sfn|Oyatsuhime Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987|p=46-47}}. However, the Chigi of the left wakimiya (Isotake no Mikoto) is a soto-kege, and the chigi of the right wakimiya (Miyatomatohime no Mikoto) is an inward-kege.

== Ritual organization ==

== Shinto priest ==
The priesthood of Oyatsuhime Shrine was held for {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}-{{ill|1592|Q6769|qid=Q6769}}) It is said that the Tsuchiya clan ({{ill|honsei|Q11520116|qid=Q11520116}}: Fujiwara clan) has been hereditary since around 1987|1987|p=46-47}}.

However, in the "Kiokuni Famous Places Zue," when it was compiled in the late Edo period, the Shinto priest was the Mori clan, who claimed to be a descendant of Oyahiko no Mikoto, and the current generation is the 83rd generation from Oyahiko no Mikoto.

== Parishioners ==
Oyatsuhime Shrine is said to be the local deity of six districts, including Udamori, where it is enshrined, Hironishi, Kitano, Nango, Nishitai, and Kita. |Q11454763}} was formed, but currently it only remains in the Nagaho district.

According to "Kii Zoku Fudoki", {{ill|Yabusame|Q1886157|qid=Q1886157}}, {{ill|Sarugaku|Q1204318|qid=Q1204318}} and {{ill|Dengaku|Q3022455|qid=Q3022455}} were once held as festivals on June 1st and September 21st (both according to the lunar calendar). The same book also states that the priests of Itae-so Shrine serve during the festivals held on the last day of October and November 16th (both according to the lunar calendar), and that in October they serve food such as red bean rice, persimmon mochi, fish, and sake. It is said that a {{ill|Mikoshi|Q979940|qid=Q979940}} from Itaukeso Shrine was {{ill|transferred|Q11561919|qid=Q11561919}} to our company in November.
